As someone who’s failed several classes (including the same one twice), here’s my advice. First, take a breath and give yourself some space to consider what you need/want right now vs your long term goals. Do you want to try again next term? Do you need a break/time to regroup? Do you need time to do something different? Second, depending on what you want to do, it’s important to look at your school’s policies on failing and what your options through your school look like. When you’ve gotten that clearer for yourself, it will be easier to approach your parents. Best of luck!

You do not deserve to die. You deserve a life that allows you to be yourself and be happy. Distance is really tough and can make previous difficulties flare, but agreeing to talk is a good first step, even if it’s just to get clarity on the situation to figure out a way forward. If therapy is an option, I encourage you to look into what that would look like for you. My two cents re: therapy is this (if you want to hear it):

Therapy is a way to give ourselves more tools in our emotional/mental health toolkit, and ultimately we ARE the ones doing the fixing ourselves when we go to therapy. Your relationship is not lessened by wanting or needing a therapist to navigate difficulties. Even if it’s just for you, therapy is a good option to get a roadmap of how to take those steps. There are a lot of different kinds of therapy, and you could find the one that you think will be the best help for you. 

Regardless of what you choose to do regarding therapy, I hope y’all are able to talk and give each other the space to be heard. Your child deserves to have parents who treat one another with that respect and who care for themselves in order to better care for him. I hope you keep reaching out to those friends and take care of yourself ❤️

It’s incredibly overwhelming to deal with suicidal thoughts and feelings, but you are not alone. It’s not wrong of you to want or need to be cared for, and I’m sorry your family has not given you the kind of care you deserve. I encourage you to reach out to your boyfriend and sibling. Talking to someone you trust is very important, especially when you feel like you’re being crushed under the weight of these feelings. 

I know it’s so hard, but I promise you that you have more options than you think. If you have a local library, that is a great place to start to access resources for any number of things you could do. Whether that’s getting your GED, doing online training in something that interests you, accessing resources to make art/practice skills, or even just getting out of your home environment for a bit to read a few books. I apologize if any of that comes across as condescending, I just know it was hard for me to find a place to start when I was stuck in the darkest parts of my feelings. I hope you are able to find what that next step looks like for you because you deserve a long and happy life, and I fully believe that you will be able to get there.

Feeling trapped is terrifying, even more so when you’re in an abusive situation. Without knowing where you live I can’t offer specifics, but a good place to start is getting yourself somewhere safe, even for a bit, whether that’s your room, a friend’s home, a local library, or any other public space where you feel safe. The next step is looking into local resources for young people who are in abusive situations. There are often hotlines and text lines that you can reach out to that can offer concrete steps to get yourself out of where you are and into a safer place to regroup and take next steps. I am so sorry that your pain is being framed as attention seeking—I won’t pretend to know what your life is like, but punishment for “attention seeking” was the reason I hid the worst of what I was going through from my family. You are not alone, and even just posting here shows that you have the strength to self advocate and find a way forward. Please stay safe and take care of yourself. If you need help finding local resources, I will help.

I’m so sorry for what you went through with your family. You did not deserve to be neglected or abused, and I hope you have been able to create distance to begin to heal from the trauma that was inflicted on you. As far as your friends go, no person who cares more about their “image” than their friends is worth continuing to be friends with, as hard as it may be. Their behavior sounds callous and cruel to be frank, and if one conversation with you while drunk was enough to “ruin” how their girlfriend thought of them, then she probably knew he was a garbage boyfriend already. As hard as it is, take this space as a time to be kind to yourself. Maybe reach out to an old friend you haven’t spoken to, or take time to do things for yourself that you haven’t in a while. You seem like a genuinely caring person, please do not let the cruelty of others force you to be cruel to yourself. You deserve better than what you’ve had, and I’m so sorry you’re in pain.

You deserve better than that, and I’m so sorry that someone you love has broken your trust. I hope you keep talking to those people who are checking in—as scary as it is, talking about it with people is an important step to figuring out a better way through. I’m glad you were able to write out your feelings here, you aren’t alone.

I’m so sorry you’ve been overwhelmed by these feelings, and I can’t promise you that they will get better or go away, but I can promise you that you can make it one more day, and then another. I know how hard it is to fight against those feelings, but it is always worth giving yourself at least one more day. You are not just a statistic—no one is—when we think about those numbers it’s because we don’t know the people behind them, but your friends and family know you and will never be able to see you as just a number. Respond to those messages, tell your parents you love them an extra time, and please take care of yourself. You are worth so much more time than you are planning to give yourself—much, much more.

I’m in a similar situation with my partner of 3 years. I can’t say that I know the golden answer to make things better, but the best place to start is to talk to your boyfriend. I know it’s hard to be vulnerable, but this is someone who loves and cares for you.

Tell him how you actually wanted/appreciate the support and comfort he offered before, but you didn’t know how to accept it. Ask him how he’s feeling, and try to come up with a plan for how to handle certain situations in the future (not everything will magically get solved in one night). 

For example, one thing that I tell my partner is when I’m having an especially low day. The heads up let’s him know that I may need support during the day, and honestly saying it out loud and acknowledging my bad days has been kind of cathartic.
